faqs.q: Sec. 54-281. - Valet parking operation on public right-of-way or in public facilities.
faqs.a:
Valet parking services may operate upon or using a public right-of-way or facility
               if all of the following conditions are met prior to the start of valet operations:
(a)
A conditional use permit must be requested by the valet parking services operator
                  and issued by the traffic engineer;
(b)
The drop-off and pick-up 'valet stand' location must be approved by the traffic engineer.
                  The number of spaces allowed for use may not use more than the number of spaces as
                  designated by the traffic engineer;
(c)
Vehicles, persons, or equipment associated with the valet operation may not impact
                  or impede pedestrian or vehicle traffic flow or create pedestrian or traffic hazards;
(d)
Valet equipment located within a sidewalk or other public pedestrian path must be
                  located so that the minimum width for an accessible route required by the State of
                  Colorado, City of Arvada, and Americans with Disabilities Act;
(e)
The city may temporarily suspend the valet service if it is deemed by the traffic
                  engineer or a peace officer to be impeding foot or vehicular traffic or otherwise
                  negatively impacting traffic conditions. Valet service may not resume until the operation
                  is corrected in a manner that is deemed acceptable to the city;
(f)
Temporary suspension or relocation of the valet stand may be required at the direction
                  of the traffic engineer in order to facilitate any local street closures, maintenance,
                  repairs, or other unanticipated circumstances which may arise;
(g)
On-street parking spaces shall not be used for parking of vehicles by the valet operator;
(h)
The valet operator shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the City for any legal
                  actions, judgments, claims, costs or expenses against the valet operator that occur
                  as result of the valet operator's operation. This includes circumstances that arise
                  from a vehicle being located in the public right-of-way or in the City's parking facilities
                  when the valet operator has control of a vehicle resulting from their operations;
                  and
(i)
Off-street parking areas shall not be blocked off or reserved for the exclusive use
                  of the valet operator unless arrangements have been made and agreed upon by the city.
(
Ord. No. 4561, § 2, 8-29-2016
)
